title: Measurement-free Preparation of Surface-Code States with Digital-Analog Counterdiabatic Drivings
authors: Shubham Kumar Balaganchi A. Bhargava, Paolo A. Erdman, Anne-Maria Visuri, Jose D. Martın-Guerrero, Yolanda Vives-Gilabert, Enrique Solano, Narendra N. Hegade
abstract: Preparing stabilizer-code states with shallow circuits is an important primitive for near-term quantum error correction in superconducting circuits, where logical-state initialization requires four-body stabilizer correlations from native one- and two-body controls. We introduce a digital-analog method for the preparation of surface-code ground-state manifolds. The method exploits a structural property of the adiabatic gauge potential, mapping stabilizer-local counterdiabatic terms to digital-analog blocks on the superconducting layout using fixed-angle two-qubit \(XY\) gates, single-qubit rotations, and analog exchange-interaction evolutions. The dressed blocks generate higher-order operators used as the variational ansatz to determine the counterdiabatic terms within the Sels-Polkovnikov adiabatic-gauge-potential framework. We benchmark checkerboard plaquette-stabilizer grids up to \(4\times4\), the square-grid instances correspond to rotated surface codes, while the rectangular cases probe the scaling of the method. For all grids, the proposed method generates the dominant four-body counterdiabatic basis and, at short evolution times substantially improves the ground-state preparation as compared with bare adiabatic evolution. We further generalize the construction to \(n\times m\) stabilizer lattices and show that digital-analog synthesis can reduce the entangling depth by an order of magnitude. Together, these results establish a direct connection between stabilizer geometry, the structure of the counterdiabatic gauge potential, and digital-analog control for measurement-free preparation of stabilizer-code states on near-term superconducting architecture.
summary: This work details a novel digital-analog technique to prepare stabilizer-code states in superconducting circuits without measurement. By synthesizing high-order Pauli operators using only native two-qubit interactions and digital dressing, the method significantly improves state preparation fidelity over standard adiabatic or fully digital approaches. This establishes a direct link between stabilizer geometry and scalable quantum control for near-term quantum error correction.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of preparing stabilizer-code ground-state manifolds, a crucial step for near-term quantum error correction.
main_result: The proposed digital-analog method successfully generates the necessary high-order counterdiabatic basis and substantially improves ground-state preparation fidelity compared to bare adiabatic evolution.
method: It employs Counterdiabatic (CD) driving, synthesizing the required higher-order Pauli operators using a digital-analog approach that combines native analog exchange interactions with short digital dressing layers.
model_or_system: The model is based on superconducting circuits implementing surface-code-like stabilizer states, tested on checkerboard plaquette grids up to $4	imes4$. The dynamics are governed by an interpolating Hamiltonian driven by the CD term derived from the adiabatic gauge potential.
key_observables: Ground-state fidelity ($F_{	ext{GS}}$) and ground-state energy ($E_0$).
important_parameters: System size ($n 	imes m$ grids), time evolution ($t$), and error parameters ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the structural property of the adiabatic gauge potential can be exploited, and it provides an effective resource-level description rather than a full gate-resolved simulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the surface-code benchmark geometry, the state-preparation path, and the digital-analog construction on a superconducting qubit processor grid.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the CD driving framework, presents the digital-analog synthesis technique using matching sets, benchmarks the method on increasing lattice sizes, and compares resource costs and fidelity against other CD protocols.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, hardware-aware protocol for achieving complex quantum states (stabilizer codes) by mapping abstract theoretical requirements (CD terms) onto physically realizable, native qubit interactions.

FIG. 2. Digital-analog construction for higher-order Hamiltonian ansatz. A two-dimensional superconducting-qubit processor is modeled as a grid of transmon qubits connected by tunable couplers. Activating the couplers generates native XY -exchange interactions on the hardware graph. Digital dressing layers, built from fixed-angle two-qubit XY -type gates (red curves) and single-qubit rotations, are applied on a matching set consisting of disjoint edges. Conjugating the native exchange block sequentially by these matching-dependent dressing circuits generates a structured pool of multi-body Pauli operators relevant to plaquette-local CD synthesis.
